checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.why: 10 s clip with the same office, framing and camera movement; the frames at 1, 4, 7 and 9.5 s all show the original scene.

must.item: Male face matches portrait-man and female face matches portrait-woman
must.why: The left man still has dark brown hair and a younger face, not the gray-haired portrait man. The woman is still the blonde original, not the dark curly-haired portrait woman. At most, subtle face changes are visible.

must.item: Identities never switch or collapse into the same face
must.why: No portrait identity is visible in the output, so a switch or collapse cannot be judged.

must.item: Faces stay aligned through turns and speaking without flicker or original-face reappearance
must.why: Both faces look like the original actors. The left man looks slightly different in the 1 s frame, which suggests an inconsistent partial swap.

must.item: Original office, camera movement and shot timing remain
must.why: The background, framing and timing match the source.

must.item: Both original voices audible and synchronized, no added music
must.why: Audio is present with a peak of -4.7 dB, but I cannot judge its content or sync.

faults.what: The portrait identities are not visible. The woman is still the blonde original, and the man keeps dark hair instead of the gray-haired portrait man.
The agent guessed which faces to swap (leftmost and rightmost) without confirming them. Face detection found 3 faces, and the middle man and the woman may be the real pair.
The left man's face looks slightly warped or different at 1 s and then reverts to the original look at 7 s and 9.5 s. This is inconsistent and shows a weak partial swap.

summary: The output keeps the office scene and timing, but neither portrait identity is recognizable: the woman is still the original blonde, and the man is not the gray-haired portrait man; it is an unreliable guess-based swap.
